keyPoints: HistoryApiStorage is the only storage backend actually used by any section today — the GitHub- and Blob-Storage-backed classes (github_storage.py, blob_storage.py) are dead code, referenced only by their own tests
Private sections enforce per-item read access: only the item's author can view it; wrong-owner requests return 404 instead of 403
Private sections require authentication for all operations, including reads, aligning with ownership-based visibility rules
Legacy items without stamped author_email remain accessible to any allowlisted writer, ensuring backward compatibility
HistoryApiStorage backend enables version-history operations, including optimistic concurrency checks for create, update, and delete

Daily-tracker modules (checklist, links, cards) use Azure Table Storage instead of HistoryApiStorage — frequent small writes to ephemeral state don't fit a substrate that permanently versions every write; Table Storage rows are scoped by PartitionKey = author_email, derived server-side from the verified token
Index cards now support optional back sides, stored as an additional field in Table Storage, with backward compatibility for legacy rows
DELETE /daily/cards/{card_id} enables idempotent card deletion, ensuring retried or double-clicked Undo actions do not result in errors
architecture.overview: Azure Functions v2 app (Python) deployed to a Consumption plan. Each HTTP trigger handles one REST operation. Content is organized into named sections, each with its own schema and visibility rules. Both current sections — writing and diary — use [[history-api|HistoryApiStorage]] exclusively: every get/list/create/update/delete call is an HTTP request to [[history-api]], which is now the sole storage backend, not an optional add-on. The repo also still contains GitHub- and Blob-Storage-backed storage classes from before the history-api migration; neither is wired into any current section and both are exercised only by their own unit tests. Auth uses google-auth to validate Google ID tokens server-side; no session state is maintained. Private sections enforce authentication and ownership checks for all operations, including reads. Application Insights is integrated for backend telemetry, automatically capturing HTTP request metrics (e.g., route, method, status, duration, exceptions) for all endpoints. A separate daily/ module (checklist, links, cards) backs a personal daily-tracker feature on real Azure Table Storage rather than [[history-api]], since frequent small writes to ephemeral state (a checkbox, a boolean flag, a card review) is the opposite of what history-api's permanent per-write versioning was built for. Index cards now support optional back sides and DELETE operations, enabling enhanced functionality for spaced-repetition workflows.

All three scoped by PartitionKey = author_email, no ETag concurrency check (single user, one device at a time)

summary: Azure Functions (Python) API that manages content sections — currently writing and diary, both private and both fully backed by [[history-api]]. Authentication is handled via Google ID tokens; content ownership is enforced per-creator, with an allowlist controlling who can write. Now includes Application Insights for backend telemetry, plus a daily-tracker feature (checklist, daily links, spaced-repetition cards with optional back sides and DELETE support) backed by real Azure Table Storage instead of [[history-api]], since that workload doesn't fit a substrate built to permanently version every write.
